topic: Eclipse 2026-08-12 magnetic-bucket results draft rev3 (EXP-687-rev3) - cycle-3 frozen-prediction deep-attack review
proposal_verdict: REVISE (targeted, rev4) - not publish-ready. Do not integrate verdicts, do not commit predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results.json, do not OTS.
current_verdict_holds_note: No verdict is integrated; all four magnetic predictions stay pending. 'false' means the draft's proposed PRED-095 failure_attribution and the WIN-010 profile scored_result do not hold as written.
our_argument_summary: Rev3 closes most cycle-2 holes and adds three things: power against the dome formula's own per-station amplitudes, a scored WIN-010 site-registered profile test (dome-favourable against our binary profile), and a reproduction of the dome's BOU quiet test. The contact-phase (PRED-TIER-1) conclusion is robust and its 'model' attribution is supportable. Four problems block publication. (1) PRED-095's attribution to the dome author's representation rests on a wrong description of the dome's arithmetic: the -17..-21 range is the formula with the 1.672 factor applied once, not twice (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:75-76; monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:prediction_level.PRED_095.failure_attribution_note). (2) The draft calls the BOU-formula amplitudes 'not robustly tested' while its own joint 8-station fit rejects them at 4.1 standard errors or more (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_win010_profile.json). (3) The time-shift control used to deny the dome credit for the WIN-010 profile result is selectively reported and confounded. (4) The quadratic-trend 'mostly curvature' reading is not established, because the injection test cannot detect template-shape absorption.

holes_found.description: PRED-095's failure_attribution misdescribes the dome's arithmetic and is too generous to the model as a result. The draft says 'the -17..-21 figure is the BOU formula with kappa applied a second time' (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:prediction_level.PRED_095.failure_attribution_note; the same wording is in the headline-level attribution text and in symmetric_labelling_options.option_A.consequences). The dome's own text says: 'Magnitude: -17 to -21 nT at stations with >80% coverage (×1.672 correction applied 2026-03-28)' (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:75-76). It also says: 'Required action: Multiply all BOU-baseline predictions (E001-E009 BOU column) by 1.67' (monitor/baseline/05-model.txt:475), and gives 1.672 = 18.22/10.9 (03-predictions.txt:882). -10.9 × cov × FSF × 1.672 gives EBR -17.82, SPT -16.42, COI -16.93 and HAD -21.45. That is the range, with ONE application of the factor. The dome does label its correction factor 'κ' (:76: 'correction factor 1.672 = κ = 1.67 nT/µGal to 3 decimal places'). That equation is its own numerology problem, but it is still a single multiplication. The double application is real only for the live monitor.py -28.9 nT (18.22 × 0.95 × 1.672), which the draft itself documents correctly in dome_live_scoring_entry.kappa_double_application. Our own pending EXP-684 also says '~-17.8 after x1.672; -17 to -21 range; -28.9 monitor.py with the double-applied 1.672' (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-684.json). The attribution rule in predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-erratum-2026-09-27.json:attribution_rule attributes a miss to the MODEL when the value 'follows from that model's stated mechanism and parameters, as its proponent specified them'. The ×1.672 recalibration is the proponent's own pre-event, model-level specification. At the ×1.672 per-station amplitudes (priority stations: EBR -17.8, SPT -16.4, HAD -21.4, CLF -16.9, NGK -11.1, ESK -17.3), the test already has 3-sigma power of 0.84-1.00: this is the draft's own PRED095_-17 column. So under the dome's current specification, the PRED-095 miss is a MODEL failure (as-if). The draft instead attributes it to 'analyst_representation (dome-author side)', which shields the model on the strength of a misdescribed derivation. A defender who noticed the error could use it to discredit the whole attribution scheme. It also misstates what the dome says.
holes_found.recommendation: Delete 'kappa applied a second time' everywhere it refers to -17..-21. State that the dome published two pre-event specifications of the same formula: the uncorrected -10.9 baseline (formula_runtime.json at the pinned SHA, used in our frozen B2-M-001) and the ×1.672-corrected baseline (predictions page prose, 2026-03-28, with the explicit instruction to rescale all BOU predictions). Report power and attribution under BOTH: corrected → testable and absent → failure_attribution model (as-if); uncorrected → see C3-2. Note in the results file that erratum symmetry_obligation (OTS-stamped, cannot be edited) framed 'the dome's own formula' with the -10.9 baseline only. The results file supplements it; it does not contradict it. Update Option A/B consequences and both proposed notes accordingly.

holes_found.description: The draft calls the BOU-formula (-10.9) amplitudes 'NOT ROBUSTLY TESTED' and, in both proposed notes, says they 'were not detectable that day' (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:z_component_evaluation.power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.summary.obscuration_shaped_BOU; prediction_level.PRED_095.proposed_note_option_A/B; headline). Its own WIN-010 profile block contains a joint 8-station test of exactly that amplitude, and it is not used. The profile fit is residual = ΔZ/(-10.9 × coverage^alpha) regressed on the dome's FSF values (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:scripts.rev3_win010_profile.py), so k = 1 IS the dome formula at the BOU baseline. Re-fitted in this review from the published residuals: dome coverage, alpha 1, tau 0, linear trend gives k = 0.524 ± 0.116, so k = 1 is 4.1 se away (chi2 21.5 at k = 1 vs 4.77 at best fit, 8 stations). Ephemeris coverage, linear: k = 0.382 ± 0.083, 7.4 se. Quadratic trend: 13.5 se (dome coverage) and 18.3 se (ephemeris). tau 30, linear: 4.2 se. At the ×1.672 specification: 9.9-33 se. The per-station power table is weak because each station has one noisy fit. The joint fit pools eight stations and has the power the erratum asked for. Both directions matter. The same block shows a latitude-ordered negative Z residual at about half the formula amplitude (k/se 4.5, linear trend), which is dome-favourable in shape and dome-unfavourable in size, and the headline reports only the shape.
holes_found.recommendation: Add the joint-amplitude test to power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes as the primary formula-amplitude test (post hoc, preregistered:false). Calibrate it empirically: the WLS se assumes independent station noise, and storm-recovery external fields are spatially correlated. Report the distribution of fitted k over the 19 control days and quote (1 - k_event) against that spread. If k = 1 stays excluded at >= 3 control-calibrated SD in the linear variant, replace 'not robustly tested / not detectable that day' with 'rejected jointly at the -10.9 baseline amplitude; a latitude-ordered residual at about 0.5× (linear) / 0.16× (quadratic) that amplitude is present'. Put both halves in the headline.

holes_found.description: The WIN-010 profile result is set aside ('NOT attributable to the eclipse', monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:site_registered_tests.WIN_010_profile.scored_result) mainly because of one post-hoc time shift, and that shift is selectively reported and confounded. (a) Selective reporting: monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_profile_shift.json also contains +180 min (FSF k/se +0.99 linear, +1.58 quadratic), which is back to null and is omitted from controls.time_shift and the headline. Only -240/-180/-120/+120 are quoted. (b) Sign: +120 is OPPOSITE in sign (k/se -6.31) and a poor fit for both profiles (chi2 25.0 FSF / 39.6 binary; quadratic 51.5 / 72.0). An opposite-signed, badly-fitting structure is not shown to be the 'leading edge' of the in-window same-sign residual. (c) Contamination: the shifted window is w = [C1-60, C4+60] + 120 min. For EBR (C1 17:36, C4 19:21, skyfield DE421 this run) that is about 18:36-22:21 UT. The window starts while EBR, SPT and HAD are still eclipsed (their C4 is 19:08-19:21). It spans the sunset/terminator passage, and it contains the dome's global C4 at 21:01 (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:191-195). 'Two hours after the eclipse, when no station was eclipsed' is therefore not accurate. For standard physics the window may also hold post-eclipse Sq-recovery transients, which could plausibly be opposite-signed. (d) No calibration: the shift was run on the eclipse day only. How often ordinary days show |k/se| >= 6 in the same evening window is unknown, so its evidential weight is unknown. (e) The registered discrimination statistic is not unusual. Δchi2(binary - FSF) on the event is 7.22, and 2 of 19 control days equal or exceed it; FSF wins on 12 of 19 control days (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_profile_ctl.json summary). The unusual quantity is the FSF-scaled AMPLITUDE (k/se 4.32; 0 of 19), not the profile preference. Also, the draft says 'by our own pre-registered rule the discrimination is robust'. The pre-registered alpha rule (EXP-684 prose: 'If the ranking ... holds across that range, the linear-coverage approximation is adequate') tests whether the coverage approximation is adequate. It does not test whether the discrimination is diagnostic. (f) Exploratory check in this review (post hoc, computed from outputs.rev3_win010_profile.json residuals plus DE421 solar elevations): FSF is barely distinguishable from a FLAT profile. The chi2 values are 3.94 vs 5.51 (ephemeris coverage, linear), 4.77 vs 8.15 (dome coverage, linear) and 6.30 vs 11.10 (ephemeris coverage, quadratic). A sin(solar elevation) profile fits as well or better on the ephemeris/linear variant (chi2 2.98). For a sunset eclipse, solar elevation increases northward (EBR 4.6 deg, LER 14.2 deg), so standard Sq physics also expects larger eclipse effects at the northern stations. In short, what failed is our binary step profile (its out-of-band suppression). FSF did not win against magnetic-latitude or standard physics in general. Symmetry test: had our profile won by 0/19 control days, a single opposite-signed +120 shift would not have been accepted as grounds to deny our credit.
holes_found.recommendation: Rewrite scored_result as: 'Our pre-registered binary profile FAILED (failure_attribution analyst_representation, stated first and plainly). A latitude-ordered negative Z residual at ~0.5× the formula amplitude (linear trend) coincided with the eclipse window (0/19 control days); its cause is unresolved (eclipse Sq depletion weighted by solar elevation, storm-recovery external field, or chance at ~1/20), and its amplitude rejects the dome formula (C3-2). The data do not discriminate FSF from a flat or solar-elevation-weighted profile. Neither side is credited.' Replace 'NOT attributable to the eclipse' with 'not established as eclipse-caused'. Either report all computed shifts (including +180), run the same shifted windows on the 19 control days, and use a shift set whose windows do not overlap local C1-C4 at any station and exclude 21:01 - or demote the time-shift to a limit. Fix the headline sentence to match.

holes_found.description: 'The rev2 Z-down shape was mostly late-afternoon curvature' (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:z_component_evaluation.sensitivity_table.conclusion; EXP-687-rev3 C2-4 resolution; headline 'with a quadratic trend they are absent at 5 of 6 priority stations') is not established. The injection power in monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:scripts.rev3_fits.py adds av×tp and refits with the SAME template tp as a regressor. By linearity of least squares, the recovered coefficient is then unbiased regardless of the trend terms, so the test cannot detect a real signal of different shape being absorbed by the u² term. In a synthetic check in this review (idealised obscuration bump; C1 17:32, max 18:29, C4 19:22; window C1-60..C4+60), the tau-0 template's partial correlation with u² (given 1, u) is -0.70. A true response lagged by 20 / 30 / 60 min (the typical ionospheric lag range) is recovered at 0.75 / 0.58 / 0.32 of its peak with the quadratic trend, versus 0.94 / 0.82 / 0.56 with a linear trend. So the quadratic variant can absorb 25-40% of a realistically lagged eclipse response. The ASC control supports curvature at non-eclipsed longitudes. It does not show that the eclipse-station fits are ONLY curvature. This matters in both directions: it inflates the quadratic-variant consistency_z against dome amplitudes, and it weakens our own 'non-eclipse' reading.
holes_found.recommendation: Run a mismatch-injection test on the real null days: inject responses with lags of 0/15/30/60 min (exponential relaxation), fit with the tau-0 and tau-30 templates under linear and quadratic trends, and publish the recovered-fraction table. Restate as: 'consistent with late-afternoon curvature; not separable from a lagged eclipse response at this noise level'. Qualify the quadratic-variant rows of power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes by the recovered fraction.

holes_found.description: The sensitivity conclusion contradicts its own table, and the formula-amplitude power is shown for one pulse width only. The conclusion says 'Contact-phase: survives every variant at every priority station (power 1.0 local; >= 0.88 global at 2-5 sigma except ESK global at 5 sigma 0.88)' (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:z_component_evaluation.sensitivity_table.conclusion). The rows show min_power_m17_any_threshold of 0.74 at EBR c14_local, 0.36 at HAD c14_global and 0.20 at ESK c14_global. control_station_check.pre_C1_step also says '(power >= 0.88)'. power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes exists only at sigma = 10 min, yet the headline says the formula's smaller amplitudes 'would still have been detectable' in a sentence about 'every pulse width and trend model we tried'. At non-priority stations the global-contact power at BOU amplitudes is 0.28 (LER) and 0.56 (GUI). The contact-phase conclusion survives at 3 sigma and sigma 10 min. The prose overstates its generality. Carry-over of C2-4 residue.
holes_found.recommendation: Correct the conclusion to the table minima. Either extend power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes to sigma 3-30 min or limit the headline claim to 'at a 10-min pulse width'. List LER/GUI global-contact power in a footnote.

holes_found.description: Overgeneralisation on our side about the dome's BOU quiet test. The draft says 'the test cannot certify ANY summer day as quiet' (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:conditions.dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev.control_context). It also says 'would void a Northern-summer eclipse regardless of geomagnetic activity' and 'the BOU-stdev rule would void any Northern-summer event' (symmetric_labelling_options.option_B.consequences), and EXP-687-rev3 anticipated_objections uses the same claim. Independent recomputation in this review (BGS GIN BOU 1-min, same statistic) finds solar-minimum summer days that pass: 2019-07-12 4.17 nT, 2019-08-25 4.82 nT, 2020-07-15 4.62 nT. The claim holds for July-August 2026 (near solar maximum), not for Northern summers in general. It is the rhetorical basis for calling the rule an 'unconditional escape clause', and a defender can refute it with public data.
holes_found.recommendation: Restrict to: 'no day from 2026-07-13 to 08-12 passes (5.49-15.21 nT), including Kp-1 days; in this high-activity summer the statistic is dominated by Sq. In solar-minimum summers some days pass (e.g., 2019-07-12, 4.17 nT).' Soften 'unconditional escape clause for this event' to 'an escape clause that no day of this season could satisfy'. Keep the exact-reproduction credit.

holes_found.description: PRED-TIER-1's 'model' attribution rests mainly on contact-phase timing. The dome text allows a defender to dispute that the timing clause is part of Tier 1. The contact-phase paragraph sits in the κ-coupling preamble (03-predictions.txt:104). The Tier-1 block itself is headed 'Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible)' and asks for 'r > 0.7 with umbra contact geometry' (:106-109). A defender can read Tier 1 as the obscuration-shaped signal, with contact-phase timing belonging to the coupled gravity tiers. Under that reading the draft's own r > 0.5 clause is NOT met (6/6 stations). The attribution must then rest on amplitude.
holes_found.recommendation: State the Tier-1 attribution under both readings. Contact-phase reading: absent with power. Obscuration reading: the -17..-21 amplitude is absent with power 0.84-1.00, and the joint fit rejects both the ×1.672 and the -10.9 formula amplitudes (C3-2), even though the r > 0.5 shape clause is met. Model attribution then survives either reading, and the draft should say so explicitly.

holes_found.description: Reproducibility of what would be OTS-anchored. The 2026 INTERMAGNET inputs are best-avail/Provisional: the BOU 2026-08-12 header fetched this run reads 'Data Type Provisional'. Definitive data will replace them, and no input-file hashes are recorded in _meta.reproducibility or in either bundle. The draft was also hand-edited after build_rev3.py ran (_meta.post_build_edits), and the bundle's build_rev3.py includes only the second edit. Anchoring outputs whose inputs can change and cannot be re-derived byte-for-byte is the same weakness our Timestamp Error tab criticises.
holes_found.recommendation: Before any OTS stamp: record the sha256 and publicationState of every input file (or archive the inputs under predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-results-inputs/), rerun build_rev3.py so the draft is exactly its output, and note that definitive-data re-runs are expected to shift values slightly.

holes_found.description: Dome-favourable credit is incomplete in the headline. It reports that the day failed the dome's BOU quiet test, but not that the dome's statistic is well-defined and exactly reproducible (2.23/8.05/5.59 from public data). That is genuine credit, and it is listed only in dome_favourable_findings[7]. The WIN-010 sentence also leads with a 'but' clause before our own failure is stated. Compare how the Hartland sentence is written: 'failed ... That is our error'.
holes_found.recommendation: Headline: '(the dome's quiet statistic is exactly reproducible from its published values)'. Then: 'Our pre-registered binary profile failed this test - our error; the residual's cause is unresolved.'

stronger_arguments.description: Use the joint 8-station amplitude fit, not per-station power, to test the dome formula. It pools the stations, uses the dome's own FSF shape, and rejects both published baselines (the -10.9 API baseline at >= 4.1 se, the ×1.672 prose baseline at >= 9.9 se, linear trend). This is cleaner and more symmetric than 'variant-dependent'.

Resolve the WIN-010 profile result by shape non-discrimination rather than a time shift. FSF correlates with CGM latitude at r = 0.99 across these stations, it fits only marginally better than a flat profile, and a solar-elevation-weighted profile (the standard-physics expectation for a sunset eclipse) fits about as well. What failed is our step profile; nothing was won by FSF physics.
sources: this review's post-hoc exploratory fit (computed from monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_win010_profile.json residuals + skyfield DE421 solar elevations)

stronger_arguments.description: For PRED-095, cite the dome's own pre-event instruction to rescale all BOU predictions by 1.67 (05-model.txt:473-475). This makes the -17..-21 range unambiguously the proponent's specification, so the erratum rule assigns a miss to the model.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right that 2026-08-12 failed its own quiet criterion, and that criterion is well-defined and exactly reproducible: BOU whole-day Z standard deviation gives the dome's published 2.23/8.05/5.59 nT (independently recomputed this run from BGS GIN data; monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:conditions.dome_own_quiet_test_BOU_stdev). It is also right that the eclipse-window Z residuals across its stations increase with latitude in its FSF ordering, more strongly than on any of 19 control days (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_profile_ctl.json, control_dome_kz_ge_event = 0).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The latitude ordering has the right shape but half the size. The joint fit gives k = 0.52 ± 0.12 of the -10.9-baseline formula and rejects the formula's amplitude at >= 4 se (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-rev3-scripts-20260928.json:outputs.rev3_win010_profile.json). The ×1.672 amplitude the dome actually published for 2026 (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt:75-76) is rejected at ~10 se. The contact-phase signature the dome calls ECM-unique is absent at all six priority stations with power at 10-min pulse widths (monitor/analyst/analysis-records/eclipse-2026-08-12-magnetic-results-DRAFT-20260928T054604.json:z_component_evaluation.power_at_dome_formula_amplitudes.summary.contact_phase). A tan(latitude) ordering is also what a sunset eclipse would produce under standard Sq physics, because solar elevation rose northward (4.6 deg at EBR, 14.2 deg at LER). Being right about the ordering therefore does not favour dome physics.

exp684_crosscheck_for_q609: EXP-684 pre-event framing: 'Kim & Chang ... most conspicuous at magnetic latitudes of 30-50°' and 'the robust out-of-band set is narrowed to LER+ESK' (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-684.json). Rev3 finds ESK and LER carry the LARGEST residuals under both coverage inputs, the opposite of the ≤30% suppression. The post-event paragraph must state that our binary profile failed. Without that, the pre-event sentences read as though the expectation held.
EXP-684 'crude but falsifiable nine-number competitor' stays accurate, and it was in effect falsified. Keep the phrase, but it must be followed by the result.

EXP-684 correctly describes the dome's baselines ('~-17.8 after x1.672; -17 to -21 range; -28.9 monitor.py with the double-applied 1.672'). Rev3's PRED-095 note contradicts it. Align rev3 to EXP-684 (C3-1), not the reverse.

EXP-684's alpha rule ('If the ranking ... holds, the linear-coverage approximation is adequate') is correct. Rev3's gloss 'by our own pre-registered rule the discrimination is robust' misreads it (C3-3e). EXP-684 should not adopt rev3's gloss.
If EXP-684 cites Kim & Chang for the 30-50° band, the 2026 result together with the ISS-3101/E-2 citation review means the post-event text should not present that band as confirmed for this event.

WIN-010.c17 (queue 609, reviewed earlier today) already flags a Chapman (1933) mis-citation and a stale '15 October' patch. Integrate the WIN-010 post-event paragraph only after rev4 fixes C3-3's scored_result wording.

deeper_analysis: Priority of fixes: C3-1 and C3-2 together flip PRED-095's attribution from 'analyst_representation' to 'model' under the dome's own current specification. They also replace 'not robustly tested' with a joint-fit rejection. This makes the result harder on the dome, but only because the draft's generosity rested on an arithmetic error and an unused test. The review applies the same discipline to our side: C3-3 and C3-4 remove two arguments the draft used in our favour (the +120 shift and 'mostly curvature'), and C3-6 removes an overgeneralisation used against the dome's quiet rule. After rev4 the magnetic story should be: the contact-phase signature is absent with power; the dome's amplitude (either specification) is rejected jointly; a latitude-ordered residual at a fraction of that amplitude coincided with the eclipse, cause unresolved; our binary profile failed; our B1-M-001 was non-diagnostic as registered; and both sides' preconditions failed. Counter-consideration: the joint k test is itself post hoc and relies on the WLS/independence assumption. If the control-day calibration (C3-2 recommendation) shows k scattering by ±0.5 on ordinary days, the rejection weakens to ~1 SD and 'not robustly tested' becomes defensible again. In that case the draft should say so with the calibration shown, not by per-station power alone.

summary_for_decider: Cycle 3 on EXP-687 rev3: REVISE (targeted, rev4). 1 critical, 3 major, 4 moderate, 5 minor. C3-1 (critical): PRED-095 is attributed away from the model because '-17..-21 = kappa applied twice'. That is wrong: the dome applied ×1.672 once (03-predictions.txt:75-76; 05-model.txt:475), and 'twice' applies only to monitor.py -28.9. Under the erratum rule this is a model failure (as-if), with power 0.84-1.00. C3-2 (major): 'BOU-formula amplitudes not robustly tested' is contradicted by rev3's own joint fit (k = 0.52 ± 0.12; formula k = 1 rejected at >= 4.1 se); calibrate against control days. C3-3 (major): the WIN-010 time-shift control omits +180, uses an opposite-signed poorly fitting +120 window that overlaps the eclipse, global C4 21:01 and sunset, and has no control-day calibration. Rewrite as 'our profile failed; cause unresolved; FSF not distinguishable from a flat or solar-elevation profile'. C3-4 (major): the quadratic-trend 'mostly curvature' reading is untested, because the injection uses the same template; synthetic lag-30 recovery is 58%. Moderates: sensitivity prose vs table; the 'any summer' quiet-test overclaim is refuted (2019-07-12 4.17 nT passes); Tier-1 attribution needed under both readings; inputs unhashed/provisional. Carry-overs: ISS-3088 (label vocabulary), ISS-3103 (sensitivity). Our-side recomputations confirmed: BOU stdev 2.23/8.05/5.59/7.62, Hartland 94.37%, WLS fits, 8/8 bundle hashes. Keep all four predictions pending; no results-file commit; no OTS. Route to analyst as an EXP-687 rev4 continuation; the next curmudgeon pass is cycle 4 (deep-attack). EXP-684/q609 cross-check notes are in other_focus_checks.
